newsitem.title: USA: Hartford mulling new arena to retain hockey team.
newsitem.headline: Hartford mulling new arena to retain hockey team.

text.p: City officials have not ruled out building a new arena downtown for the National Hockey League Hartford Whalers, Mayor Mike Peters said in an interview broadcast on local radio Thursday.
The Whalers have said the state must build a new arena, costing as much as $240 million in taxpayers' money, if it wants the team to stay in Connecticut.

Gov. John Rowland has said a new arena would be too expensive at a time when state officials are trying to craft a tight budget for the new fiscal year that begins July 1. But Peters said he and Rowland were working to keep the Whalers in the city.
"We're trying to figure out exactly what we have to do to keep them here," said Peters. "I'd be an idiot to want to lose the Hartford Whalers - I'm a big fan of theirs."
He also said the team's economic importance to downtown was "phenomenal."
Peters said Hartford officials were not out of the loop despite the fact that the state has the stronger hand in dealing with the Whalers. One idea being mulled is
retrofitting the Civic Center with more luxury boxes, said Peters.
Another possibility was to build a new arena downtown and turn the Civic Center into a convention center, he said.
Peters said no plan to use taxpayers' dollars would be approved without a long-term guarantee from the team that it would remain in Hartford.
